conversation.user: Who is Stacy D. VanDeveer and what research did he lead at SSL?
conversation.assistant: Regarding who Stacy D. VanDeveer is, the available documents do not provide biographical information or a professional title beyond identifying him as a principal investigator [1]. Stacy D. VanDeveer served as the principal investigator for a research project titled "Learning from the Massachusetts Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness (MVP) Program in the Greater Boston Region" [1]. The objective of this study was to understand conditions in and across municipalities [1].

conversation.user: What was the research on the Massachusetts MVP program about?
conversation.assistant: The research project titled "Learning from the Massachusetts Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness (MVP) Program in the Greater Boston Region" had the objective of understanding conditions in and across municipalities [1]. The study included findings from the Basic Municipal Vulnerability Assessment for Climate Change Adaptation in the Greater Boston Metropolitan Area [1]. As of 2020, more than 80% of Massachusetts cities and towns had participated in the MVP program, and the research findings are being used to improve the program's design for equitable inclusion [1].

conversation.user: What is the East Boston study that VanDeveer's team worked on?
conversation.assistant: The research project titled "Conditions and Recommendations for Equitable Climate Resilience in East Boston" examines environmental justice concerns and seeks to generate a better understanding of how these concerns apply to climate planning for residents through a justice lens. The study utilizes a framework of just adaptation and involves secondary document analysis of existing resilience plans, with recommendations developed through partnerships with residents and organizations. Although this project is listed within the section of the annual report dedicated to Stacy D. VanDeveer [1], Patricio Belloy, a student working with Professor VanDeveer, completed an assessment of resilience planning in East Boston through a climate justice lens [2].
